headline: Light rain and mountain snow arrive this afternoon and evening, but the bigger story is a stormier stretch starting Tuesday with repeated rounds of rain, mountain snow, gusty winds and a growing coastal flooding threat.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Morning fog, freezing in spots where temperatures sat near freezing, gradually burns off Saturday as mid- and high-level clouds increase over the north Olympic Peninsula and Puget Sound lowlands. Highs reach the mid 40s to near 50. Light rain reaches the coast this afternoon and spreads into the interior this evening, with light snow in the mountains.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: A low-pressure system parked offshore keeps light rain going into Sunday, but amounts stay small: a tenth to a quarter inch along the coast and only a few hundredths inland, with many interior spots staying dry. Snow levels hover around 2,000–3,000 feet, giving the Cascade passes less than half an inch of snow. Monday brings another round of precipitation focused mainly on the Olympic Peninsula, with 4–8 inches of snow possible in the Olympic Mountains. Highs Sunday and Monday are in the mid 40s to low 50s.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A deepening low offshore Monday night into Tuesday turns the pattern much more active, sending several storm systems across western Washington. Expect multiple rounds of widespread lowland rain, mountain snow and gusty winds starting Tuesday and lasting through the second half of the week. Rivers will start to rise; widespread river flooding is not expected, but the Skokomish River will likely reach flood stage late in the week.

coast: High monthly tides could bring some minor coastal flooding along the Pacific coast and the Strait of Juan de Fuca by Sunday. Tuesday's storm brings another round of high surf to the coast, and high tides combined with the stormy weather raise the coastal flood threat later in the week, especially on the Pacific coast during high surf. On the water, winds of about 23–35 mph (20–30 knots) affect the coastal waters and the east Strait of Juan de Fuca today into Sunday, with Small Craft Advisories for the Strait and coastal waters (until 4 PM today for the central and west Strait, until 4 AM Sunday for the east Strait and coastal waters) and a Gale Warning until 4 PM today for the outer waters from Cape Flattery to James Island. Gale-force gusts are likely in the coastal waters and part of the east Strait Monday through Wednesday, with a 20–40% chance of storm-force gusts; seas build from 8–12 feet today to 16–20 feet Monday before easing to 10–14 feet late in the week.
watch_for: Possible minor coastal flooding along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Pacific coast by Sunday, with a larger coastal flood threat Tuesday onward.
The stormy stretch from Tuesday through late week: widespread rain, mountain snow and gusty winds.
The Skokomish River, which will likely reach flood stage late in the week.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in light, mostly coastal rain through Sunday and in a turn to a much stormier pattern from Tuesday, though they give few specifics yet on amounts and wind strength for later in the week.
